facts.name: On-campus research MS
facts.detail: The on-campus Computer Science M.S. is described as research-focused training in theory, systems, and applications.
facts.quote: The on-campus Master of Science program in computer science provides rigorous, research-focused training in theory, systems and applications, preparing you to advance the frontiers of computing

facts.name: Distinct from the MCS
facts.detail: The page distinguishes this research M.S. from the industry-oriented Master of Computer Science.
facts.quote: Unlike the industry-oriented Master of Computer Science program, the MS program in computer science emphasizes fundamental and applied research.

facts.name: Location and college
facts.detail: The degree is listed at the Tempe campus in the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.
facts.quote: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering

facts.name: 30 credit hours
facts.detail: The program is listed as 30 credit hours.
facts.quote: 30 credit hours

facts.name: Thesis or nonthesis option
facts.detail: Students may choose a thesis or nonthesis culminating experience.
facts.quote: You may pursue either a thesis or nonthesis option as your culminating experience and can explore advanced topics such as:

facts.name: Advanced topic areas
facts.detail: Listed topic areas include AI, cybersecurity, quantum computing, and related areas.
facts.quote: including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, quantum computing and other novel paradigms.

facts.name: STEM-OPT eligible
facts.detail: The program page marks the degree as STEM-OPT extension eligible.
facts.quote: STEM-OPT extension eligible: Yes

facts.name: STEM-OPT length
facts.detail: The page says F-1 students can extend U.S. work experience by 24 months.
facts.quote: International students (F1) can extend U.S. work experience by 24 months.

facts.name: Handbook program summary
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 M.S. handbook describes a 30-credit program with a computing and AI foundation.
facts.quote: The Master of Science in Computer Science is a 30-credit hour program that provides students with a comprehensive foundation in computer science and AI

facts.name: Six concentrations
facts.detail: The handbook lists a generic program plus five named concentrations.
facts.quote: The MS in CS program offers six concentrations:

facts.name: Graduate College and Fulton requirements
facts.detail: Applicants must meet Graduate College and Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering requirements.
facts.quote: Applicants must fulfill the requirements of both the Graduate College and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.

facts.name: Prior degree field
facts.detail: Applicants need a bachelor's or master's in computer science, computer engineering, or a closely related area.
facts.quote: Applicants are eligible to apply to the program if they have earned a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, computer engineering or a closely related area from a regionally accredited institution.

facts.name: GPA 3.25
facts.detail: The degree page requires a minimum 3.25 GPA in the last 60 hours of the first bachelor's degree or in an applicable master's program.
facts.quote: Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in the last 60 hours of their first bachelor's degree program or a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 (scale is 4.00 = "A") in an applicable master's degree program.

facts.name: Application materials
facts.detail: Required materials include the graduate application and fee, official transcripts, a statement of purpose, and proof of English proficiency.
facts.quote: All applicants must submit:

facts.name: Calculus prerequisite
facts.detail: Students must have completed two semesters or six credit hours of calculus, equivalent to Calculus I and II, before applying.
facts.quote: Before applying to the program, students must have completed two semesters or six credit hours of calculus, equivalent to Calculus I and II.

facts.name: Discrete math recommended on degree page
facts.detail: The degree page recommends a discrete math course before admission.
facts.quote: Completion of a discrete math course is also recommended before admission.

facts.name: Discrete math required in handbook
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 handbook states a background in discrete math is required for admission.
facts.quote: A background in discrete math is required for admission

facts.name: Deficiency courses
facts.detail: Assigned additional undergraduate courses may include CSE 230, CSE 310, CSE 330, and CSE 340 or CSE 355.
facts.quote: CSE 230 Computer Organization and Assembly Language Programming

facts.name: Deficiency grade and timing
facts.detail: Assigned additional coursework must be completed with a C or higher within two semesters of admission, according to the degree page.
facts.quote: Students assigned any additional coursework upon admission must complete those classes with a grade of "C" (scale is 4.00 = "A") or higher within two semesters of admission.

facts.name: Letters of recommendation not required
facts.detail: The SCAI graduate CS page says letters of recommendation are not required for the Computer Science MCS/MS program.
facts.quote: Letters of Recommendation are not required for students applying to the Computer Science MCS/MS program.

facts.name: GRE not required
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 handbook states GRE scores are not required.
facts.quote: GRE scores are not required.

facts.name: Handbook GPA
facts.detail: The handbook requires a minimum 3.25 GPA in the last 60 undergraduate credit hours.
facts.quote: To be considered for the MS program, we require a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.25 in the last 60 credit hours of the undergraduate degree.

facts.name: English proficiency
facts.detail: The handbook lists English proficiency minimums, including IELTS 6.5.
facts.quote: Applicants demonstrate proficiency by scoring at least 80 (if taken before January 21, 2026) or 4 (if taken on or after January 21, 2026) on the TOEFL iBT, 6.5 on the IELTS, or 105 on the Duolingo English test.

facts.name: Program options
facts.detail: The degree can be completed as a course-based master's, with a thesis, or with the applied project course CSE 593.
facts.quote: 30 credit hours - course-based master's, or 30 credit hours and a thesis, or 30 credit hours including the required applied project course (CSE 593)

facts.name: Required core areas
facts.detail: All options require 9 credit hours in the core areas of applications, foundations, and systems.
facts.quote: Required Core Areas (9 credit hours)

facts.name: Course-based electives
facts.detail: The course-based option includes 21 credit hours of electives.
facts.quote: Students in the course-based option take 21 credit hours of electives.

facts.name: Thesis electives
facts.detail: Thesis students take 15 credit hours of electives.
facts.quote: Students in the thesis option take 15 credit hours of electives.

facts.name: Applied project electives
facts.detail: Applied project students take 18 credit hours of electives.
facts.quote: Applied project students take 18 credit hours of electives.

facts.name: CSE 593 Applied Project
facts.detail: The applied project culminating course is CSE 593 (3 credit hours).
facts.quote: CSE 593 Applied Project (3)

facts.name: CSE 599 Thesis
facts.detail: The thesis culminating course is CSE 599 (6 credit hours).
facts.quote: CSE 599 Thesis (6)

facts.name: 500-level CSE minimum
facts.detail: At least 24 of the 30 credit hours must be 500-level CSE courses at ASU.
facts.quote: At least 24 of these credit hours must be 500-level CSE courses at ASU.

facts.name: 400-level limit
facts.detail: Up to six credit hours of 400-level courses may be applied to the plan of study.
facts.quote: Up to six credit hours of 400-level courses may be applied to the plan of study.

facts.name: AI concentration courses
facts.detail: The handbook lists CSE 571, CSE 575, CSE 576, and CSE 574 as required AI concentration courses.
facts.quote: CSE 571 Artificial Intelligence (3)

facts.name: Cybersecurity concentration course
facts.detail: The handbook requires CSE 543 Information Assurance and Security in the cybersecurity concentration.
facts.quote: CSE 543: Information Assurance and Security (3)

facts.name: Fall priority deadline
facts.detail: The degree page lists a Fall in-person priority deadline of 12/01.

facts.name: Spring priority deadline
facts.detail: The degree page lists a Spring in-person priority deadline of 08/01.

facts.name: Priority deadline meaning
facts.detail: Applications completed before the priority deadline receive priority consideration; later applications are reviewed in order and on a space-available basis.
facts.quote: A priority deadline means that applications submitted and completed before the priority deadline will receive priority consideration.

facts.name: Handbook deadlines
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 handbook lists December 1 for a Fall start and August 1 for a Spring start.
facts.quote: December 1 for Fall start

facts.name: SCAI deadline table
facts.detail: The SCAI graduate CS page lists December 1 for the M.S. or M.C.S. Fall deadline.
facts.quote: December 1 (MS or MCS) or

facts.name: TA application for master's students
facts.detail: The assistantships page says master's students may apply for Spring 2027 TA, IA, or Grader positions, with a November 7 priority deadline.
facts.quote: The application for spring 2027 TA, IA or Grader positions available for graduate students are now open. Priority deadline is November 7.

facts.name: TA awards emphasis
facts.detail: The same page states that TA positions are awarded to highly qualified PhD students.
facts.quote: TA positions are awarded to highly qualified PhD students.
